dedupe_keys.name: global high resolution soil profile database for crop modelling soilgrids for dssat 10 km

description: This database gives soil profiles in the DSSAT crop model format (*.SOL) for each country at 5 arc-minute (about 10 km) resolution, so that crop models can run on a global grid. The Dataverse page says soil properties (bulk density, organic carbon, clay and silt, pH and cation exchange capacity) come from SoilGrids 1 km and ISRIC-AfSIS, hydraulic properties such as field capacity and wilting point were derived with a pedo-transfer function, other inputs follow the HarvestChoice HC27 database, and uncertainty maps are given for organic carbon and wilting point water content in the top 15 cm. It was made by the International Research Institute for Climate and Society, Michigan State University and HarvestChoice at IFPRI, first released on 15 October 2015 and updated to version 2.7 on 18 June 2025, as a by-country archive of about 320 MB, a point shapefile, the uncertainty archive and a working paper, downloadable and free under the IFPRI datasets terms of use. Coverage is global. Caveats: properties are modelled from SoilGrids 2014, not measured, and evaluation was only visual comparison with other maps. For simulation it supplies the soil inputs that DSSAT and similar crop models need for gridded yield, drought and irrigation demand scenarios. Related catalogue records include DSSAT and APSIM.
